summary: MPP natively binds payee and amount, makes challenges single use, and returns receipts. Budgets, consent, identity, revocation and disputes come from rails or from tools around the protocol. The best places for an independent controls layer are the client just before the SDK signs (mppx runs extensions there), the session channel inventory, and receipt reconciliation after the fact.

native.note: The core payment is pseudonymous with an optional DID source; mppx adds RFC 9421 request attestation for Web Bot Auth and Visa TAP, and the card method allows optional TAP headers.
No agent registry in MPP, and the core forbids requiring accounts for payment; any know-your-customer step belongs to a method, and the stripe method needs Stripe accounts on both sides.
Browser wallets should show the origin and ask for explicit confirmation; SPT creation may prompt 3DS or biometrics. No user mandate object.
Caps come from the rail: the session deposit, SPT usage limits, Tempo access key limits. The core has none.
recipient and realm are bound into the challenge id; SPTs are scoped to the seller networkId; v2 session descriptors must match the payee.

Challenges carry expires, subscriptions subscriptionExpires and SPTs expires_at. Tempo session channels and vouchers never expire, as in the EVM and Hedera drafts; XRPL channels can carry Expiration or CancelAfter, and Solana sessions have idle timeouts and an optional voucher expiresAt.
No core revocation message; subscriptions cancel by method-specific means and a payer can force-close a channel.
Method-specific: Stripe may prompt 3DS while creating an SPT; card methods carry network cryptograms.
Single-use challenge ids and proofs, Idempotency-Key, digest binding, and channel and EIP-712 domain binding in sessions.

Payment-Receipt with a method reference, recommended by the core and required on every successful payment by the Tempo, stripe and card charge drafts and the Tempo session draft; session receipts add spent and acceptedCumulative, and a streamed response also ends with a receipt.
Depends on the rail: card and stripe routes keep chargebacks; Stripe stablecoin payments have no disputes; on-chain charges are final.

No reputation layer. The discovery draft's informative guidance lets aggregators add trust scores, uptime and volume data, and its comparison with prior art says the draft is compatible with future on-chain anchoring, naming the ERC-8004 registries.
Public explorer data (MPPscan, Tempo chain) and the Stripe Dashboard for Stripe-settled payments; servers should rate-limit.

No protocol stop. A payer stops signing or force-closes a channel, a Tempo account holder revokes access keys through the AccountKeychain precompile, and the agent side that issued an SPT can revoke it before the seller uses it.

gaps.title: No user mandate
gaps.description: MPP has no object that records what a user allowed an agent to buy; AP2 or wallet policy must supply it.

gaps.title: No protocol budget
gaps.description: Limits exist only in rails (deposit, SPT, access keys) and SDK hooks.

gaps.title: No native agent identity
gaps.description: The core carries only an optional payer identifier. Request attestation is an mppx feature, not part of the core draft, and the card method lets a client add TAP signature headers.

gaps.title: Tempo channels without expiry
gaps.description: Open Tempo session channels and unsettled vouchers persist until closed, as in the EVM and Hedera drafts; all three only advise servers to close channels idle for about 30 days or more. XRPL channels can expire, and Solana sessions use idle timeouts.

gaps.title: Rail-dependent disputes
gaps.description: Stablecoin charges have no chargeback; refunds are seller policy.

controlPoints.what: Decide whether to pay: recipient allowlists, price ceilings, method preference.
controlPoints.how: Accept-Payment ordering plus a policy check on the decoded challenge; mppx extensions run before signing.
Small session deposits, SPT usage limits, Tempo access key limits, short expires.
Web Bot Auth or TAP attestation through mppx; Retry-After; 403 for policy denials after valid payment.

Stripe fraud tools for Stripe-settled payments. On Tempo, each token's issuer chooses its allow or block list in the Tempo Policy Registry (TIP-403); a seller can set a receive policy that limits which tokens and senders it accepts, and a blocked payment still succeeds but is held in ReceivePolicyGuard to be claimed later.
Store receipts, reconcile with chain data or the Stripe Dashboard, force-close idle channels.

checklist.item: Check amount, recipient, currency and expires before paying; ignore description.
checklist.why: Binding does not stop a dishonest server.

checklist.item: Never log credentials; keep them in memory.
Send no-store on 402 and private on paid responses.
checklist.why: Shared caches do not protect Payment-Authorization.

checklist.item: Run the latest mppx (0.14.1 on 2026-10-21); 0.8.2 fixed the last published mppx advisory. Run Rust mpp 0.12.0 or later and pympp 0.10.1 or later.
checklist.why: Earlier versions have published advisories, including payment bypasses, and mppx fixed further replay bugs without an advisory in 0.8.7 and 0.13.2.

checklist.item: Cap session deposits and track every open channel.
checklist.why: Tempo session channels never expire, and the deposit is the worst case.
Proof-of-concept attacks in 2026 mppx and pympp advisories made a sponsoring server pay about 5 to 9 times the normal fee.

checklist.item: Use digest for requests with bodies.
checklist.why: Ties the payment to the exact request.
